correctness.rationale: The blockwise Hilbert comparison gives the bound sqrt(2) and Hilbert isomorphism; ℓ2 sum of two-dimensional smooth strictly convex blocks and their Hölder duals is smooth, LUR and reflexive. The LUR local-symmetry lemma is proved by norming-functionals, midpoint convergence, and the norm-distance >=1 imposed by Birkhoff orthogonality. Explicit vectors in each ℓp block satisfy exact j(u)(v)=0 and j(v)(u)=r_p; exponential estimates give sqrt(p)(1-r_p)->1. Because X and X* are strictly convex, no Birkhoff pair has reverse residual 1. Reflexive smooth duality transfers the same residual to X*. The checker reproduces exact rational cancellations and inequalities, but analytic arguments supply the infinite statements. The separate nonuniform-convexity claim follows from pairs 2^{-1/p_n}(1,±1) on the p_n-block: distances tend to 2 and midpoint norms to 1.
risks: The arithmetic checker tests finite exponents only; infinite claims are established by the support formula and LUR proof, not enumeration.
The Hilbert equivalence is at most sqrt(2); optimal Banach-Mazur distance is not claimed.

originality.rationale: The claim deliberately excludes novelty of a smooth infinite-dimensional failure of global C approximate symmetry: Chmieliński--Wójcik 2018 Example 3.7 already contains that, as directly acknowledged by the original 2020 arXiv full text. The finer phenomenon verified here is a specific Hilbert-equivalent primal/dual LUR and smooth pair, with both uniform local direction bounds at every nonzero point, exact nonattained maximal support defect, and a quantified explicit asymptotic sequence. Neither the full 2020 text nor the indexed comparable results gives this conjunction. The 2018 full text remained inaccessible and is named as a serious residual risk rather than declared not covering. The complete public proof of “Zero Birkhoff saturation without an extremal pair in a reflexive strictly convex space” has been inspected. Its \(\ell_2\) sum of \(\ell_{1+1/k}^2\) is isometric to the dual in this finding, but it proves James-type saturation with coordinate witnesses, not C-approximate support-functional asymmetry; thus same-space overlap has been explicitly compared at statement/implication level.
residual_risks: The full 2018 Chmieliński--Wójcik Example 3.7 could already use a Hilbert-equivalent LUR norm or otherwise imply the strengthened configuration; the original source was not fully accessible for decisive exclusion.
Earlier but unindexed formulations may express the same local-versus-global phenomenon using support functional angles or James orthogonality.
No independent human originality assessment has been performed.

value.rationale: Global C-approximate symmetry is guaranteed by uniform convexity but fails here on a Hilbert-renormable, separable reflexive LUR/smooth space and its LUR/smooth dual, even though every vector in both spaces enjoys both locally uniform directional C-bounds. This structurally separates local rotundity from global uniformity. The exact support defects approach the maximal boundary nonattained at rate p^{-1/2}, giving a reusable asymptotic witness rather than a negative statement without mechanism.
risks: The construction is not uniformly convex in the chosen equivalent norm; it does not refute the established uniformly convex positive theorem.
Significance of the strengthened example depends on whether an equivalent construction appears in the inaccessible 2018 predecessor.
